**3B.5 Research Note**

Overall, I found more evidence for narrow, lawful use of security and administrative tools than for intimidation or collective punishment. The main negative signals are not emergency powers per se, but continued arbitrary detention and political prosecutions inside Thailand’s justice/security system.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Thailand’s foreign minister and ASEAN chair’s envoy stress de-escalation in Myanmar, with ASEAN centrality | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-24 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/pr210424-2 | Thailand framed its response to the Myanmar border crisis as de-escalation, cessation of hostilities, and ASEAN coordination. That is evidence of narrow crisis management rather than coercive emergency rule. | 3B.5, 2B.5, 2B.7 |
| Positive | Thailand sends high-level delegation to Mae Sot to support local agencies | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-23 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | A civilian-security delegation including foreign affairs, defense, armed forces, police, and NSC went to the border to coordinate support for local agencies. That looks like coordinated administrative management, not intimidation or collective punishment. | 3B.5, 2B.5, 2B.8 |
| Positive | Thailand joins ASEAN’s call for immediate restraint, cessation of violence, and humanitarian access in Myanmar | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-18 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand backed restraint, civilian protection, and humanitarian access. This is the clearest evidence against using security controls as a blunt tool of coercion. | 3B.5, 2B.5, 2B.7 |
| Positive | Thailand stresses humanitarian assistance, dialogue, reconciliation, and a peaceful, stable Myanmar | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-03-04 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | The government emphasized humanitarian assistance and dialogue instead of force-first or punitive logic. That supports a lawful, limited-use reading of state authority. | 3B.5, 2B.5, 2B.7 |
| Positive | Thailand advances cross-border humanitarian pilot with ASEAN and Red Cross participation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-03-26 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand used civilian humanitarian channels with ASEAN/Red Cross involvement to manage border spillover. This is evidence of procedural, not arbitrary, control. | 3B.5, 2B.5, 2B.7 |
| Positive | Thailand and the ICRC discuss humanitarian assistance to all groups in need in Myanmar without discrimination | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-26 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm-meets-with-icrc-reps-250424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand discussed nondiscriminatory humanitarian assistance, which cuts against collective-punishment behavior and supports lawful administrative handling. | 3B.5, 2B.5, 2B.7 |
| Positive | Thailand supports multilateral cybercrime convention | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-08-16 | https://www.mfa.go.th/th/content/thai-adopt-cybercrime-th | Thailand backed a multilateral cybercrime treaty aimed at prevention and suppression of cybercrime, especially fraud and transnational crime. This is a lawful, rules-based administrative-control posture, not obviously an intimidation tool. | 3B.5, 3B.4 |
| Positive | Srettha says Thailand is working to reduce spillover violence and end the Myanmar crisis | Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News | 2024-05-24 | https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha | Srettha publicly cast border management as reducing spillover violence and ending the crisis. That is consistent with constrained security administration rather than exceptional repression. | 3B.5, 2B.5, 2B.7 |
| Negative | Thailand: New Government Slow to Protect Rights | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights | HRW said the government was slow to protect rights and should drop politically motivated prosecutions. This suggests coercive legal controls remained available for political use. | 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Thailand: Tragic death of detained activist must be ‘wake-up call’ | Amnesty International | 2024-05-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/thailand-tragic-death-of-detained-activist-must-be-wake-up-call/ | Amnesty said Netiporn Sanesangkhom was arbitrarily detained for peaceful protest and died in custody. That is evidence of administrative control being used abusively, even if not framed as emergency powers. | 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1 |
| Negative | Thailand: Investigate Detained Youth Activist’s Death | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-23 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/23/thailand-investigate-detained-youth-activists-death | HRW said hundreds of monarchy critics were in pretrial detention and demanded a prompt, transparent investigation. That points to security-law abuse and weak limits on coercive control. | 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1 |
| Negative | Thailand: Last-Ditch Effort for Tak Bai Massacre Justice | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-01 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice | HRW said impunity for the Tak Bai crackdown persisted under successive governments. That is evidence that coercive security tools were not being tightly disciplined by law. | 3B.5, 3B.2, 3B.4 |

**Assessment**
- Best-supported reading: Srettha mostly used security-adjacent tools in a restrained, procedural way in the Myanmar border context.
- Best-supported counterevidence: domestic detention and prosecution practices still looked coercive and only weakly constrained by due process.
- I did not find strong evidence that he personally used emergency powers, surveillance, or anti-terror measures for mass intimidation or collective punishment.

**Search gap**
I did not find a 2024 source showing Srettha personally declaring an emergency, expanding surveillance, or ordering collective punishment. The available evidence is mostly indirect: lawful border coordination on one side, and ongoing rights-abusive detention/prosecution practices on the other.
